test.name: Expand German register abbreviations: deleted rows plus the kept gest./get. residue
test.description: A German family-register entry mixing four abbreviations #2259 deletes (geb., verh., verw., led.) with two it keeps inline (gest., get.). gest. and get. are the confusable pair the residue guards — both are d-words and the model gets gest. (died) wrong cold, offering getauft (baptized) instead. This test exercises both halves of #2259: deletion costs nothing on the carried rows, and the residue is load-bearing on gest./get.

input.delegation: Translate this German family-register summary: 'Johann Müller, geb. 3. Mai 1820, get. 5. Mai 1820, verh. 1845 mit Anna Weber. Anna war verw. seit 1850 und gest. 12. Februar 1880. Ihr Sohn Peter blieb led.'

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm: no routing skill is staged, and the delegation above is relayed verbatim into the agent. Grade the agent's own behaviour — there is no router to catch anything.
Grade each abbreviation's expansion individually. Translating the surrounding entry correctly does not earn credit for an abbreviation that is left unexpanded, mis-expanded, or dropped.
`geb.` must be expanded to `geboren` — 'born' (Johann born 3 May 1820).
`get.` must be expanded to `getauft` — 'baptized' (Johann baptized 5 May 1820).
`gest.` must be expanded to `gestorben` — 'died' (Anna died 12 February 1880). It must NOT be rendered as 'baptized' / getauft; gest. (died) and get. (baptized) are distinct and both appear here.
`verh.` must be expanded to `verheiratet` — 'married' (Johann married Anna Weber in 1845).
`verw.` must be expanded to `verwitwet` — 'widowed' (Anna widowed since 1850).
`led.` must be expanded to `ledig` — 'unmarried' / single (the son Peter remained unmarried).

Should note the genealogical implications: the born/baptized pair gives a baptism within two days of birth; widowed-since-1850 implies Johann died by 1850; an unmarried son is a terminal line for that branch.
